data.claim: One port suffices: outbound adapters only post and report pending, the harness bridge couriers and reads through attest, the terminal collects; services/ask relays every collected answer through engine.answer, which already holds the digest and identity checks, so no adapter repeats them. No second notifier exists in ddflow today.
data.falsifier: An existing notify-send, osascript or smtplib implementation in ddflow, or a wire format of a target that cannot be expressed as one JSON POST with an optional bearer header.
data.mechanism: adapters is the bottom layer and cannot import the engine, so a channel returns data (Answer) and a service above records it. engine.answer refuses an actor whose source is not terminal, credential or named, and compares the presented digest with the row's. attest already records harness answers at level 2, so the bridge calls it rather than repeating it.

data.probe_output: grep exit 1 (no match). engine.answer: 'if actor.source not in ANSWER_SOURCES: raise AskRefused', _check_answerable compares digest != row['digest']. Slack: POST {"text": ...}, 200 'ok'. Teams: Office 365 connectors retired May 2026; Workflows webhook takes {"type":"message","attachments":[{contentType adaptive card}]}. OpenClaw: POST /hooks/agent {"message", "name"}, Authorization: Bearer hook token, query tokens rejected, 200 admitted.
data.question: Can one HumanChannel port (notify, ask, relay) cover terminal, harness bridge, desktop, email, Slack, Teams, webhook, n8n and OpenClaw, keeping the digest and person-only checks in the ask engine alone, with no existing notifier to fold in?

evidence.note: Research note recorded for ADP-notify-ask, CONFIRMED: grep for notify-send, osascript and smtplib in ddflow exits 1; engine.answer holds the digest and identity checks; Slack, Teams and OpenClaw wire formats read from their docs, each one JSON POST.

data.body: Split out of ADP-notify-ask so the port touched only its own files (r-adapters): a [notify] section needs config/_core.py, config/__init__.py, README.md and the goldens, all held by other lanes when it landed. (1) A [notify] section (channel, ask_channel, endpoints, token_env, send_timeout_s, ask_timeout_s, ask_attempts, email_host, email_port, email_from, email_to, email_user, email_password_env, email_tls) with the defaults of channels.Settings, a knob_added manifest each, README knob rows, goldens; channel and ask_channel are enums with the adapters as choices and the network ones outward. Settings.committed is derived from cfg.sources: every field whose source is 'file'. Acceptance: open_channel reads the knobs; an address set in the committed layer makes its adapter unavailable. (2) channels.grant_consent has no command: approval.grant is a person's terminal act, and r-approval-chat-channel wants a chat route. Add a gated site row and a verb so `approvals ask` and `attest` can grant consent for one kind, keeping consent once per kind (D-adapters-answers-3). r-consent-outward says consent expires; D-adapters-answers-3 says once per kind: ask the operator whether a kind's consent expires. Until this lands every network adapter reports unavailable.
data.title: [notify] knobs that fill services/ask/channels.Settings, and a chat route to grant a channel consent

data.summary: services/waiting.standing keeps a widening wait alive while the same lease lives and its globs are not all held. After `update --globs ... --queue` was refused and a later `update --globs` dropped the wanted files, the record stayed: brief showed ADP-notify-ask waiting 3463s for CE-defaults-file, a false cycle, and sw-cedefaults queued behind a request nobody wants. Only a release ends it; there is no withdraw verb.

chunk_findings.detail: `_say` evaluates `self._out or sys.stderr`; when `sys.stderr` is `None` (possible when stderr is closed at process start or in a frozen/GUI/MCP launcher without fd 2), this is `None`, and `print(..., file=None)` writes to `sys.stdout`. In an MCP stdio server `sys.stdout` is the JSON-RPC protocol stream, so one terminal notification or question line corrupts the protocol. The channel should never fall back to stdout; it should return `Delivery(UNAVAILABLE)`/`Answer(UNAVAILABLE)` instead.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:TerminalChannel._say

chunk_findings.detail: Both methods catch only `OSError` around writes, but a closed `TextIOWrapper` such as `sys.stderr.close()` makes `print` raise `ValueError("I/O operation on closed file")`, and a non-ASCII message on an ASCII stderr raises `UnicodeEncodeError` (a `ValueError` subclass). Those propagate to the caller, violating the port contract “No method raises for the channel’s own trouble”; given `sys.stderr` closed, `TerminalChannel.notify("hi")` raises instead of returning `Delivery(UNAVAILABLE)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:TerminalChannel.notify and TerminalChannel.ask

chunk_findings.detail: On Windows, `select.select` supports only sockets, not the console file descriptor. With a real interactive `sys.stdin.isatty()`, `TerminalChannel.ask` reaches `select.select([sys.stdin], ...)`, gets an `OSError`, and catches it as `UNAVAILABLE` before reading a line. As a result the terminal adapter cannot collect an answer from a person on the standard Windows console even though a terminal is available.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:stdin_reader

chunk_findings.detail:
On macOS the message is appended to the `osascript` argv after a fixed sequence of `-e` flags with no `--` separator.  
Input: `DesktopChannel(proc, "darwin", 5).notify("-edo shell script \"touch /tmp/pwned\"", "info")`.  
`_argv` then returns `["osascript", "-e", "on run argv", "-e", "display notification ...", "-e", "end run", "-edo shell script \"touch /tmp/pwned\"", "ddflow"]`. `osascript` accepts `-e` with an attached statement, so the message is parsed as an AppleScript statement rather than the notification body; the notification is not displayed and arbitrary text can be injected into the script.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify_outbound.py DesktopChannel._argv

chunk_findings.detail: `DesktopChannel` has no `scrub` callback and never applies redaction; `notify` passes `message` directly to `_argv`. The module contract says services pass `scrub` so every word that leaves is redacted, but `DesktopChannel` cannot receive or apply a scrub. Example: a secret in a desktop notification is sent verbatim to `notify-send`/`osascript` argv despite a redacting scrub being available to the other outbound channels.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify_outbound.py DesktopChannel

chunk_findings.detail: `_as_pending` maps any non-ok `Delivery` to `Answer(UNAVAILABLE)`, discarding `FAILED`. For a `WebhookChannel.ask` where the endpoint returns HTTP 500, `WebhookChannel._send` returns `Delivery(FAILED)`, but `_as_pending` returns `Answer(UNAVAILABLE)`. That violates the file's stated D-adapters-answers-3 contract that a refusal from the other end is `FAILED`; ask/relay callers cannot distinguish refused from offline and may retry incorrectly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify_outbound.py _as_pending

chunk_findings.detail: [r-adapters] The desktop channel is built with `proc=P`, where `P` is imported directly from `ddflow.infra.proc` (line 28), not from a `ddflow/adapters` proc port. r-adapters requires subprocess tools to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`; passing `open_channel(log, cfg, "desktop")` therefore binds this service to the concrete infra implementation, so a unit test or adapter swap cannot inject a fake proc without editing this service file.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/services/ask/channels.py open_channel desktop branch / `from ...infra import proc as P`
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/channels.py open_channel desktop branch / `from ...infra import proc as P`

chunk_findings.detail: On the `got.recorded` path, `relay` only checks that a row now exists with `after["state"] == ANSWERED`. It does not compare that row against `got.text`, `got.digest`, `got.code`, `got.proof`, `got.how`, or the requested `actor`. A self-recording adapter can therefore call `engine.answer` with one answer (or fail to record and another relay can record first) but return a different `Answer(recorded=True, ...)`, and `relay` will accept and return that different answer because the only verification sees an answered state. This contradicts the module’s own claim that “the row it wrote is checked here rather than taken on its word”: the row’s contents are not checked.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/relay.py:80-84

chunk_findings.detail: `_bridge` constructs `HarnessChannel` with `payload=lambda a: {"questions": [{"question": a.text}]}`, which never includes an `options` member. `test_the_bridge_puts_a_question_as_an_ask_user_question` then calls `_bridge().ask("which?", ("a", "b"))` and evaluates `[o["label"] for o in q["options"]]`; because that payload has no `"options"`, the test raises `KeyError` and fails.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_notify.py:_bridge

chunk_findings.detail: `smtplib.SMTPNotSupportedError` is an `OSError`, so `_Smtp.__call__` raises that failure from the connection step rather than from `starttls`. Thus `test_email_never_falls_back_to_plain_text` never reaches the starttls branch; under the OSError-to-UNAVAILABLE mapping exercised by `test_email_offline_is_unavailable_and_unconfigured_too`, it returns `N.UNAVAILABLE` instead of the asserted `N.FAILED`, failing the test. The intended `starttls` raise is unreachable for this failure type.

chunk_findings.detail: `stdin_reader` treats `select` readiness as a full line. After a partial write (one character, no newline) with `timeout_s=1`, `select` returns the tty as ready and `stream.readline()` then blocks with no timeout, so `TerminalChannel.ask` never returns an `Answer` and the attempt bound is skipped. On Windows the same call raises `ValueError` from `select` on a console file (not a socket); `ask` only catches `OSError`, so the port contract that channel trouble is a status, not an exception, is broken.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:146

chunk_findings.detail: A refusal is not preserved on the question path. `_send` maps `HttpStatusError` (and other `HttpError`) to `Delivery(..., FAILED, ...)`, and `notify` returns that delivery unchanged. `ask` and `relay` always pass the result through `_as_pending`, which returns `Answer(UNAVAILABLE, ...)` whenever `done.ok` is false. Given a webhook that answers 403, `notify("x")` is `FAILED` / "the endpoint answered 403", but `ask("x")` and `relay(approval)` are `UNAVAILABLE` with the same detail. That erases the module's own split (offline `UNAVAILABLE`, refusal `FAILED`): the caller cannot tell a refused post from a channel that was never tried.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify_outbound.py:_as_pending

chunk_findings.detail: Outbound text is scrubbed only inside `_Outbound.notify` / `ask` / `relay`. `DesktopChannel` does not take `scrub` and passes the raw `message` into `notify-send` / `osascript`. Given a notify string that the configured scrubber would redact, webhook/email/slack send the redacted form and the desktop adapter shows the original. That breaks the family's rule that redaction runs on every word that leaves the process.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify_outbound.py:DesktopChannel.notify

chunk_findings.detail: When `got.recorded` is set, `relay` only checks that some later row has `state == ANSWERED` and then returns the channel’s `Answer` unchanged. It never re-reads the logged choice, digest, code, or actor, and it never runs `engine.answer`. Given a pending approval whose log is answered `"no"` (by attest or a concurrent writer) while the channel returns `Answer(status=ANSWERED, text="yes", recorded=True)`, the check passes and the caller is handed `"yes"`. That contradicts this file’s own rule that a self-vouching channel is not taken on its word, and it skips the digest, one-time code, and agent-identity checks for every adapter that sets `recorded`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/relay.py:74

titles: ddflow/services/ask/channels.py open_channel desktop branch / `from ...infra import proc as P`

chunk_findings.detail: `channel_cases(c)` iterates over fixed hardcoded expectations (`"yes"`, `"2"`, `"nope"`, `"no"`, `"free"`, `"approved"`), but the `_real` helper function provides the sequence `_terminal("yes", "2", "nope", "no", "free", "approved")`. However, `_fake` is instantiated with the same answers, and the channel cases test sequence consumes these answers in order. When the terminal implementation reads via `_lines`, the prompt asks options and parses input, but `_terminal` provides `"no"` after `"nope"` for the option checking `assert c.ask("go?", ("yes", "no")).text == "no"`, which works if `"no"` matches. But `_real` uses `_terminal` which creates a real channel where `c.ask("why?")` expects `"free"`, and `c.relay(APPROVAL)` expects `"approved"`. If a conforming adapter or a test run executes `channel_cases` with a reader that doesn't align or where input lines run out, `left.pop(0)` raises an `IndexError` (via `_lines` returning `None` or failing on `pop(0)`). Specifically, `_lines` returns `None` when `left` is empty (`left.pop(0) if left else None`), but `N.TerminalChannel`'s reader protocol expects a function `reader(timeout)` returning a string or `None`. If `reader` returns `None`, `TerminalChannel` treats it as timeout/unavailable, causing subsequent assertions in `channel_cases` (like `assert (got.status, got.text, got.how) == (N.ANSWERED, "yes", c.name)`) to fail with an `AssertionError` because `got.status` becomes `UNAVAILABLE` instead of `ANSWERED`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_notify.py:65

chunk_findings.detail: `_next` treats a scripted string as an answer only when `pick(line, options)` is truthy, then drops the string and keeps going. The module docstring says a string is what the person typed, including free text. With `answers=["not an option"]` and `ask("q", ("yes", "no"))` (or `relay`, which always passes `APPROVAL_OPTIONS`), the line is consumed, `pick` fails, and the channel returns `Answer(UNAVAILABLE, detail="the script ran out")` even though the script was not empty. A test that scripts a non-option reply therefore records an unavailable person instead of that reply.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/notify.py:50

chunk_findings.detail: `stdin_reader` only applies `timeout_s` to `select.select`, then calls `stream.readline()` with no deadline. Given a real tty, `timeout_s=1`, and the person typing `y` without a newline, `select` reports the fd ready and `readline` blocks until a newline or EOF, so `TerminalChannel.ask` / `relay` never return `UNAVAILABLE` and ignore both the timeout and `attempts`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:145

chunk_findings.detail: `_plain` keeps every `str.isprintable()` character, which includes bidi overrides such as U+202E. `relay` prints agent-controlled `approval.text` on the same lines as the digest via `approval_text`. Given text `pay Alice\u202e tsegid 999`, the terminal can show a reversed digest while `Answer.digest` stays the real one, so the person can approve a different digest than the one they read.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:152

chunk_findings.detail: `ask` and `relay` collapse every unsuccessful post into `UNAVAILABLE`. `WebhookChannel._send` (and email) already distinguish a refusal as `FAILED` — for example `HttpStatusError` becomes `Delivery(..., FAILED, "the endpoint answered 500")` — but `_as_pending` only checks `done.ok` and otherwise always returns `Answer(UNAVAILABLE, ...)`. Given a webhook that answers HTTP 500 (or SMTP that raises `SMTPException`), `notify` correctly reports `FAILED` while `ask`/`relay` report `UNAVAILABLE`, which contradicts the module’s own D-adapters-answers-3 rule that offline is `UNAVAILABLE` and a refusal from the other end is `FAILED`. Callers that retry or fail over only on “could not be tried” will treat a hard refusal as if the channel was never reached.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify_outbound.py:_as_pending

chunk_findings.detail: The self-vouch path does not check the log the way the inbound path does. `relay` treats an ask as pending only via `E.status(row, now)`, then, when `got.recorded` is set, accepts the channel if `after["state"] == ANSWERED` (the adapter constant, not `E.status`). A harness that writes a real answer whose folded status is answered but whose stored `state` is not that constant (the shape this function already refuses to trust on the way in) makes `relay` raise `AskRefused` even though the log has the answer. The inverse also passes: a row whose raw `state` equals `ANSWERED` while `E.status` is expired, refused, or a different choice than `got.text` is returned as the channel's `Answer`. The caller then observes the channel's word, not the log.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/relay.py:76

chunk_findings.detail: `stdin_reader` treats `select` readiness as a full line. After a partial write (one character, no newline) with `timeout_s=1`, `select` returns the tty as ready and `stream.readline()` then blocks with no timeout, so `TerminalChannel.ask` never returns an `Answer` and the attempt bound is skipped. chunk_findings.detail: A refusal is not preserved on the question path. `_send` maps `HttpStatusError` (and other `HttpError`) to `Delivery(..., FAILED, ...)`, and `notify` returns that delivery unchanged. `ask` and `relay` always pass the result through `_as_pending`, which returns `Answer(UNAVAILABLE, ...)` whenever `done.ok` is false. Given a webhook that answers 403, `notify("x")` is `FAILED` / "the endpoint answered 403", but `ask("x")` and `relay(approval)` are `UNAVAILABLE` with the same detail. That erases the module's own split (offline `UNAVAILABLE`, refusal `FAILED`): the caller cannot tell a refused post from a channel that was never tried.

chunk_findings.detail: Outbound text is scrubbed only inside `_Outbound.notify` / `ask` / `relay`. `DesktopChannel` does not take `scrub` and passes the raw `message` into `notify-send` / `osascript`. Given a notify string that the configured scrubber would redact, webhook/email/slack send the redacted form and the desktop adapter shows the original. That breaks the family's rule that redaction runs on every word that leaves the process.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify_outbound.py:DesktopChannel.notify

chunk_findings.detail: When `got.recorded` is set, `relay` only checks that some later row has `state == ANSWERED` and then returns the channel’s `Answer` unchanged. It never re-reads the logged choice, digest, code, or actor, and it never runs `engine.answer`. Given a pending approval whose log is answered `"no"` (by attest or a concurrent writer) while the channel returns `Answer(status=ANSWERED, text="yes", recorded=True)`, the check passes and the caller is handed `"yes"`. That contradicts this file’s own rule that a self-vouching channel is not taken on its word, and it skips the digest, one-time code, and agent-identity checks for every adapter that sets `recorded`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/relay.py:74

chunk_findings.detail: When the deadline expires, `stdin_reader` returns `None`, but any bytes the person already typed without a newline remain queued in the terminal driver. Concretely: `TerminalChannel.ask("first?")` times out after 1s while the user has typed `y`; ask reports unavailable. A later `ask("second?")` is then polluted: when the user finishes the line for the second question, the line read is `y` plus the new input (for example `yn\n`), so the channel returns an answer that did not answer the second question. A timed-out half-typed line must be flushed (e.g. `termios.tcflush`) before returning, or later questions get stale input.

chunk_findings.detail: The default desktop construction is still `proc or P`, where `P` is the direct `ddflow.infra.proc` concrete module imported at the top of this service file. The new optional `proc` keyword only helps callers that remember to pass a fake; it does not remove the default concrete dependency, so a unit test or adapter swap still cannot affect the default path without editing this service file.

chunk_findings.detail: The new read-back path overwrites `text`, `who`, `digest`, and `proof` from the log, but it does not overwrite `got.code`. chunk_findings.detail: `channel_cases(c)` iterates over fixed hardcoded expectations (`"yes"`, `"2"`, `"nope"`, `"no"`, `"free"`, `"approved"`), but the `_real` helper function provides the sequence `_terminal("yes", "2", "nope", "no", "free", "approved")`. However, `_fake` is instantiated with the same answers, and the channel cases test sequence consumes these answers in order. When the terminal implementation reads via `_lines`, the prompt asks options and parses input, but `_terminal` provides `"no"` after `"nope"` for the option checking `assert c.ask("go?", ("yes", "no")).text == "no"`, which works if `"no"` matches. But `_real` uses `_terminal` which creates a real channel where `c.ask("why?")` expects `"free"`, and `c.relay(APPROVAL)` expects `"approved"`. If a conforming adapter or a test run executes `channel_cases` with a reader that doesn't align or where input lines run out, `left.pop(0)` raises an `IndexError` (via `_lines` returning `None` or failing on `pop(0)`). Specifically, `_lines` returns `None` when `left` is empty (`left.pop(0) if left else None`), but `N.TerminalChannel`'s reader protocol expects a function `reader(timeout)` returning a string or `None`. If `reader` returns `None`, `TerminalChannel` treats it as timeout/unavailable, causing subsequent assertions in `channel_cases` (like `assert (got.status, got.text, got.how) == (N.ANSWERED, "yes", c.name)`) to fail with an `AssertionError` because `got.status` becomes `UNAVAILABLE` instead of `ANSWERED`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_next` treats a scripted string as an answer only when `pick(line, options)` is truthy, then drops the string and keeps going. The module docstring says a string is what the person typed, including free text. With `answers=["not an option"]` and `ask("q", ("yes", "no"))` (or `relay`, which always passes `APPROVAL_OPTIONS`), the line is consumed, `pick` fails, and the channel returns `Answer(UNAVAILABLE, detail="the script ran out")` even though the script was not empty. A test that scripts a non-option reply therefore records an unavailable person instead of that reply.

chunk_findings.detail: `stdin_reader` only applies `timeout_s` to `select.select`, then calls `stream.readline()` with no deadline. Given a real tty, `timeout_s=1`, and the person typing `y` without a newline, `select` reports the fd ready and `readline` blocks until a newline or EOF, so `TerminalChannel.ask` / `relay` never return `UNAVAILABLE` and ignore both the timeout and `attempts`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:145

chunk_findings.detail: `_plain` keeps every `str.isprintable()` character, which includes bidi overrides such as U+202E. `relay` prints agent-controlled `approval.text` on the same lines as the digest via `approval_text`. Given text `pay Alice\u202e tsegid 999`, the terminal can show a reversed digest while `Answer.digest` stays the real one, so the person can approve a different digest than the one they read.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:152

chunk_findings.detail: `ask` and `relay` collapse every unsuccessful post into `UNAVAILABLE`. `WebhookChannel._send` (and email) already distinguish a refusal as `FAILED` — for example `HttpStatusError` becomes `Delivery(..., FAILED, "the endpoint answered 500")` — but `_as_pending` only checks `done.ok` and otherwise always returns `Answer(UNAVAILABLE, ...)`. Given a webhook that answers HTTP 500 (or SMTP that raises `SMTPException`), `notify` correctly reports `FAILED` while `ask`/`relay` report `UNAVAILABLE`, which contradicts the module’s own D-adapters-answers-3 rule that offline is `UNAVAILABLE` and a refusal from the other end is `FAILED`. Callers that retry or fail over only on “could not be tried” will treat a hard refusal as if the channel was never reached.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify_outbound.py:_as_pending

chunk_findings.detail: The self-vouch path does not check the log the way the inbound path does. `relay` treats an ask as pending only via `E.status(row, now)`, then, when `got.recorded` is set, accepts the channel if `after["state"] == ANSWERED` (the adapter constant, not `E.status`). A harness that writes a real answer whose folded status is answered but whose stored `state` is not that constant (the shape this function already refuses to trust on the way in) makes `relay` raise `AskRefused` even though the log has the answer. The inverse also passes: a row whose raw `state` equals `ANSWERED` while `E.status` is expired, refused, or a different choice than `got.text` is returned as the channel's `Answer`. The caller then observes the channel's word, not the log.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/relay.py:76

chunk_findings.detail: The rewrite does not actually make the timeout bound the read. On a normal terminal in canonical mode, after the person types `y` without pressing Enter, `select.select` reports the fd ready because the input queue is non-empty, but the subsequent `os.read(fd, READ_BYTES)` is a blocking terminal read and will not return until a newline or EOF. Therefore `TerminalChannel.ask`/`relay` can still hang past `timeout_s` and never produce `UNAVAILABLE`. The fd is not set non-blocking, so this is the same defect as previous finding 3, just moved from `stream.readline()` to `os.read`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:stdin_reader

chunk_findings.detail:
`stdin_reader` no longer stops at one line the way `readline` did. `os.read` can return several lines in one chunk (typeahead, a paste, or a pty fed `b"yes
no
"`), the loop exits as soon as `b"
"` appears anywhere in `data`, and the function returns that whole buffer decoded. Given that input it yields `"yes
no
"` instead of `"yes
"`, so the option match fails a real `yes`, and the unread `no` is already taken off the fd, so the next `ask`/`relay` never sees it. Timeout-cut bytes are discarded the same way, with no push-back.

chunk_findings.detail: `_say` evaluates `self._out or sys.stderr`; when `sys.stderr` is `None` (possible when stderr is closed at process start or in a frozen/GUI/MCP launcher without fd 2), this is `None`, and `print(..., file=None)` writes to `sys.stdout`. In an MCP stdio server `sys.stdout` is the JSON-RPC protocol stream, so one terminal notification or question line corrupts the protocol. The channel should never fall back to stdout; it should return `Delivery(UNAVAILABLE)`/`Answer(UNAVAILABLE)` instead.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:TerminalChannel._say

chunk_findings.detail: Both methods catch only `OSError` around writes, but a closed `TextIOWrapper` such as `sys.stderr.close()` makes `print` raise `ValueError("I/O operation on closed file")`, and a non-ASCII message on an ASCII stderr raises `UnicodeEncodeError` (a `ValueError` subclass). Those propagate to the caller, violating the port contract “No method raises for the channel’s own trouble”; given `sys.stderr` closed, `TerminalChannel.notify("hi")` raises instead of returning `Delivery(UNAVAILABLE)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:TerminalChannel.notify and TerminalChannel.ask

chunk_findings.detail: On Windows, `select.select` supports only sockets, not the console file descriptor. With a real interactive `sys.stdin.isatty()`, `TerminalChannel.ask` reaches `select.select([sys.stdin], ...)`, gets an `OSError`, and catches it as `UNAVAILABLE` before reading a line. As a result the terminal adapter cannot collect an answer from a person on the standard Windows console even though a terminal is available.

chunk_findings.detail:
On macOS the message is appended to the `osascript` argv after a fixed sequence of `-e` flags with no `--` separator.  
Input: `DesktopChannel(proc, "darwin", 5).notify("-edo shell script \"touch /tmp/pwned\"", "info")`.  
`_argv` then returns `["osascript", "-e", "on run argv", "-e", "display notification ...", "-e", "end run", "-edo shell script \"touch /tmp/pwned\"", "ddflow"]`. `osascript` accepts `-e` with an attached statement, so the message is parsed as an AppleScript statement rather than the notification body; the notification is not displayed and arbitrary text can be injected into the script.

chunk_findings.detail: `DesktopChannel` has no `scrub` callback and never applies redaction; `notify` passes `message` directly to `_argv`. Example: a secret in a desktop notification is sent verbatim to `notify-send`/`osascript` argv despite a redacting scrub being available to the other outbound channels.

That contradicts this file’s own rule that a self-vouching channel is not taken on its word, and it skips the digest, one-time code, and agent-identity checks for every adapter that sets `recorded`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/relay.py:74

chunk_findings.detail: When the deadline expires, `stdin_reader` returns `None`, but any bytes the person already typed without a newline remain queued in the terminal driver. Concretely: `TerminalChannel.ask("first?")` times out after 1s while the user has typed `y`; ask reports unavailable. A later `ask("second?")` is then polluted: when the user finishes the line for the second question, the line read is `y` plus the new input (for example `yn\n`), so the channel returns an answer that did not answer the second question. A timed-out half-typed line must be flushed (e.g. `termios.tcflush`) before returning, or later questions get stale input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:stdin_reader timeout branch

chunk_findings.detail: The default desktop construction is still `proc or P`, where `P` is the direct `ddflow.infra.proc` concrete module imported at the top of this service file. Therefore the exact call that violates [r-adapters] — `open_channel(log, cfg, "desktop")` — still binds `ddflow.services.ask` to the concrete subprocess implementation instead of going through the `ddflow.adapters.proc` port. The new optional `proc` keyword only helps callers that remember to pass a fake; it does not remove the default concrete dependency, so a unit test or adapter swap still cannot affect the default path without editing this service file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/channels.py:182

chunk_findings.detail: The new read-back path overwrites `text`, `who`, `digest`, and `proof` from the log, but it does not overwrite `got.code`. A self-recording channel can still return `Answer(status=ANSWERED, recorded=True, how=<the log's via>, code="yes")` while the actual log row records code `"no"`; `_as_logged` verifies state/via and then returns `code="yes"` because `replace` preserves the channel-reported field. That leaves the logged code trusted from the channel's report, contrary to the diff’s own contract that the caller gets the row’s outcome, digest, and proof, not the report.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/relay.py:_as_logged

chunk_findings.detail: Unconditional `import termios` makes the adapter module fail to load on Windows (`ModuleNotFoundError`), so it never reaches the UNAVAILABLE status D-adapters-answers-3 already requires for that platform. Given a Windows process that imports `ddflow.adapters.notify` (or calls the terminal channel), startup raises instead of `TerminalChannel.ask`/`stdin_reader` returning unavailable; `select` never runs and the new `suppress(termios.error, OSError)` around `tcflush` is unreachable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:28

titles: ddflow/services/ask/channels.py open_channel desktop branch / `from ...infra import proc as P`

chunk_findings.detail: `channel_cases(c)` iterates over fixed hardcoded expectations (`"yes"`, `"2"`, `"nope"`, `"no"`, `"free"`, `"approved"`), but the `_real` helper function provides the sequence `_terminal("yes", "2", "nope", "no", "free", "approved")`. However, `_fake` is instantiated with the same answers, and the channel cases test sequence consumes these answers in order. When the terminal implementation reads via `_lines`, the prompt asks options and parses input, but `_terminal` provides `"no"` after `"nope"` for the option checking `assert c.ask("go?", ("yes", "no")).text == "no"`, which works if `"no"` matches. But `_real` uses `_terminal` which creates a real channel where `c.ask("why?")` expects `"free"`, and `c.relay(APPROVAL)` expects `"approved"`. If a conforming adapter or a test run executes `channel_cases` with a reader that doesn't align or where input lines run out, `left.pop(0)` raises an `IndexError` (via `_lines` returning `None` or failing on `pop(0)`). Specifically, `_lines` returns `None` when `left` is empty (`left.pop(0) if left else None`), but `N.TerminalChannel`'s reader protocol expects a function `reader(timeout)` returning a string or `None`. If `reader` returns `None`, `TerminalChannel` treats it as timeout/unavailable, causing subsequent assertions in `channel_cases` (like `assert (got.status, got.text, got.how) == (N.ANSWERED, "yes", c.name)`) to fail with an `AssertionError` because `got.status` becomes `UNAVAILABLE` instead of `ANSWERED`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_notify.py:65

chunk_findings.detail: `_next` treats a scripted string as an answer only when `pick(line, options)` is truthy, then drops the string and keeps going. The module docstring says a string is what the person typed, including free text. With `answers=["not an option"]` and `ask("q", ("yes", "no"))` (or `relay`, which always passes `APPROVAL_OPTIONS`), the line is consumed, `pick` fails, and the channel returns `Answer(UNAVAILABLE, detail="the script ran out")` even though the script was not empty. A test that scripts a non-option reply therefore records an unavailable person instead of that reply.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/notify.py:50

chunk_findings.detail: `stdin_reader` only applies `timeout_s` to `select.select`, then calls `stream.readline()` with no deadline. Given a real tty, `timeout_s=1`, and the person typing `y` without a newline, `select` reports the fd ready and `readline` blocks until a newline or EOF, so `TerminalChannel.ask` / `relay` never return `UNAVAILABLE` and ignore both the timeout and `attempts`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:145

chunk_findings.detail: `_plain` keeps every `str.isprintable()` character, which includes bidi overrides such as U+202E. `relay` prints agent-controlled `approval.text` on the same lines as the digest via `approval_text`. Given text `pay Alice\u202e tsegid 999`, the terminal can show a reversed digest while `Answer.digest` stays the real one, so the person can approve a different digest than the one they read.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:152

chunk_findings.detail: `ask` and `relay` collapse every unsuccessful post into `UNAVAILABLE`. `WebhookChannel._send` (and email) already distinguish a refusal as `FAILED` — for example `HttpStatusError` becomes `Delivery(..., FAILED, "the endpoint answered 500")` — but `_as_pending` only checks `done.ok` and otherwise always returns `Answer(UNAVAILABLE, ...)`. Given a webhook that answers HTTP 500 (or SMTP that raises `SMTPException`), `notify` correctly reports `FAILED` while `ask`/`relay` report `UNAVAILABLE`, which contradicts the module’s own D-adapters-answers-3 rule that offline is `UNAVAILABLE` and a refusal from the other end is `FAILED`. Callers that retry or fail over only on “could not be tried” will treat a hard refusal as if the channel was never reached.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify_outbound.py:_as_pending

chunk_findings.detail: The self-vouch path does not check the log the way the inbound path does. `relay` treats an ask as pending only via `E.status(row, now)`, then, when `got.recorded` is set, accepts the channel if `after["state"] == ANSWERED` (the adapter constant, not `E.status`). A harness that writes a real answer whose folded status is answered but whose stored `state` is not that constant (the shape this function already refuses to trust on the way in) makes `relay` raise `AskRefused` even though the log has the answer. The inverse also passes: a row whose raw `state` equals `ANSWERED` while `E.status` is expired, refused, or a different choice than `got.text` is returned as the channel's `Answer`. The caller then observes the channel's word, not the log.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/relay.py:76

chunk_findings.detail: The rewrite does not actually make the timeout bound the read. On a normal terminal in canonical mode, after the person types `y` without pressing Enter, `select.select` reports the fd ready because the input queue is non-empty, but the subsequent `os.read(fd, READ_BYTES)` is a blocking terminal read and will not return until a newline or EOF. Therefore `TerminalChannel.ask`/`relay` can still hang past `timeout_s` and never produce `UNAVAILABLE`. The fd is not set non-blocking, so this is the same defect as previous finding 3, just moved from `stream.readline()` to `os.read`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:stdin_reader

chunk_findings.detail:
`stdin_reader` no longer stops at one line the way `readline` did. `os.read` can return several lines in one chunk (typeahead, a paste, or a pty fed `b"yes
no
"`), the loop exits as soon as `b"
"` appears anywhere in `data`, and the function returns that whole buffer decoded. Given that input it yields `"yes
no
"` instead of `"yes
"`, so the option match fails a real `yes`, and the unread `no` is already taken off the fd, so the next `ask`/`relay` never sees it. Timeout-cut bytes are discarded the same way, with no push-back.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify.py:stdin_reader

chunk_findings.detail: `ask` and `relay` still collapse every unsuccessful post into `UNAVAILABLE`. This delta never touches `_as_pending`, so a webhook `HttpStatusError` (HTTP 500) or an SMTP `SMTPException` is still reported as `Answer(UNAVAILABLE, ...)` while `notify` reports `FAILED` for the same refusal. The confirmed probe `test_a_refused_question_is_failed_like_a_refused_notification` is not added or changed here.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/notify_outbound.py:_as_pending

chunk_findings.detail: The self-vouch path is still not checked the way the inbound path is. These commits only copy `code_presented` into the `Answer` built from the row; they do not replace `after["state"] == ANSWERED` with `E.status`. A harness that writes a real answer whose folded status is answered but whose stored `state` is not that constant still makes `relay` raise `AskRefused` even though the log already has the answer. Adding `code="LIE"` on the fake channel does not exercise or close that check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/relay.py:relay
